title: The whole admin app, every screen, the demo gym and the Hindi-English word list, downloads before the first screen shows
what: The admin app is built as one download. Every one of about 50 screens (Money, Shop, Branches, Growth, Challenges, Payments, Branding and the rest), the made-up demo gym, and the full Hinglish word list (about 135,000 characters, used only by owners who picked Hinglish) are all fetched and started before the sign-in or Today screen can draw. Only the Excel tools are fetched later. On a slow 4G phone at the front desk this makes the first open slower than it needs to be. The panel has no speed score of its own (it needs a sign-in), so the real cost in seconds is not measured.
expected: The first screen downloads only what it needs; other screens, the demo gym and the Hinglish words arrive when someone opens them.
how_often: every first open and after every update
fix_line: Load each screen, the demo gym and the Hinglish words only when they are opened, then measure the panel's first-open time on a slow phone

title: The admin app waits for Google's font list before it can draw anything
what: Before the first screen can draw, the browser must reach Google, fetch the list of three letter styles in eight weights, and only then go on. On a slow or patchy 4G connection that is an extra trip to another company's server on every cold open, and if Google is slow the whole panel waits blank.
expected: The panel's letters are served from our own site (or only the weights in use), so nothing outside our site holds up the first screen.
fix_line: Serve the fonts from our own site and keep only the weights used

title: A gym logo made from a photo is saved in the heaviest picture type, up to 1 MB
what: Every uploaded logo is shrunk to 512 pixels and then always saved as a PNG, even when the owner picked a JPEG photo with no see-through parts. A photo-style logo saved this way is often several hundred kilobytes and is allowed up to 1 MB. Each member's phone, the invite link and the gym page then download that size the first time they show the logo. The picture is kept for a year once fetched, so the cost is the first view on each phone.
expected: A logo with no see-through parts is saved in a smaller picture type, so it is tens of kilobytes, not hundreds.
who: members and visitors of the gym page
how_often: first view of the logo on each phone
fix_line: Save logos without see-through parts as WebP or JPEG and aim for under 100 KB

title: Every save rebuilds the whole gym on the desk phone, which will slow down for big, old gyms
what: After each save (a check-in, a receipt, a new member) and each change another desk sent, the admin app rebuilds the full picture of the gym: it re-sorts every member, membership, payment and every check-in ever made, then works out every member's status again. The code says a gym is small enough for this to cost nothing, but nothing measures it. A gym with 500 members checking in most days builds up well over 100,000 check-ins a year, and on a cheap desk phone each save would then pause the screen.
expected: A save only updates what changed, or the rebuild is measured on a 500-member gym with a year of check-ins and stays under a tenth of a second.
how_often: every save, getting worse as visits pile up
fix_line: Time a save on a made-up 500-member gym with a year of check-ins; if slow, update only the changed member
